object8.OCR: DECALRATION OF FRANK H. McCOURT, Jr.  I, FRANK H. McCOURT, Jr. , declare as follows:  1.  Iam the Respondent in the above- entitled action. I have firsthand, personal knowledge of the facts stated here in, and if called as a witness, I could and would competently testify there to. I submit this Declaration in support of my Order to Show Cause requesting that the Court modify the support order entered in this proceeding on June 30,2010.  As I have previously testified, Iam personally a 90% limited partner of The McCourt Broderick Limited Partnership( TMB LP) . The general partner of this partnership ( which owns the other 10% of TMB LP) is The McCourt Company, Inc. ( T MC) , which is solely owned by me. TMB LP is the ultimate owner of Los Angeles Dodgers LLC( which owns the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball club) , LA Real Estate LLC( which owns Dodger Stadium and the land beneath and immediately surrounding it) , and BlueL and co LLC( which owns approximately 250 acres surrounding Dodgers Stadium) . Attached as Exhibit“ A" and incorporated here in by reference, is a true and correct copy of an organizational chart showing the ownership of the various entities.  3.  I receive no salary from the Los Angeles Dodgers or any other entity which I own or in which I have an interest.  4.  My only source of personal cash flow is the distributions I receive from TMB LP and T MC. I receive no income or personal cash flow from any other source, other than some nominal interest from my personal bank account.  5.  The source of the distributions tome is the remainder of the rent that is paid from LA Real Estate LLC to BlueL and co LLC. LA Real Estate LLC leases the land surrounding Dodger Stadium from BlueL and co LLC. BlueL and co LLC pays the debt service on the land and sends the remainder of the rent to TMB LP as a distribution. TMB LP then contributes the rent to the various McCourt entities for payment of expenses and the remainder is paid tome, as more fully described in the declaration of Michael J. Litvack filed herewith.  6.  The rent paid by LA Real Estate LLC to BlueL and co LLC is$ 14,000,000,  Page 1 DECLARATION OF FRANK H. McCOURT, Jr.

As reported by Dr. Lawrence M. Herman in the July 20, 1972, issue of the 
Bulletin of the Los Angeles County Medical Association, "About 20% die before 
treatment can be instituted except by the patient or someone present at the 
onset."  Dr. Herman further states, "The greatest delay segment represents 
the patient decision time---the time lost before the patient decides to seek 
help."

object2.OCR:
According  to  currently  accepted  statistics,  approximately  50%  of  the  total 
deaths  from  an  acute  coronary  attack  occur  in  the  first  hour.  Pre-hospital 
mortality  from  coronary  disease  accounts  for  over  300,000  deaths  in  the  United 
States  annually,  with  some  125,000  of  those  deaths  occurring  in  the  under  65 
age  group.

object3.OCR:
Since  the  chances  of  a  coronary  accident  are  statistically  greater  in  areas 
of  high  people  concentration,  such  as  large  employee  groups,  appropriate 
responses  and  procedures  for  meeting  the  emergency  of  a  coronary  accident 
should  become  a  part  of  a  total  emergency  procedures  package,  High  rise 
buildings  offer  even  greater  challenges  to  people  charged  with  developing 
procedures  to  meet  medical  emergencies.

After more than 15 years of discussion, a fund raising policy that we believe 
to be far more comprehensive, was developed, sent to the Board, thru the regions 
and affiliates and after final revisions by the Fund Raising Advisory and Policy 
Committee, approved by the Board in June 1974.

object2.OCR:
Two years ago, the Fund Raising Advisory and Policy Committee became 
acutely aware that an average 7.7% income growth rate over the past 
five years (exclusive of 1975) is in fact a marginal real growth rate. 
In the absence of any realistic data on which to base national campaign 
goals and objectives, the Fund Raising Advisory and Policy Committee, 
along with the AHA President, asked for and received Board action on 
goals.  Specifically this action calls for all major components 
(National Office, Affiliates, Chapters, Scientific Councils, etc.) 
to set forth a statement of funds needed to support their objectives 
for 1976-'77 and '78.  Based on these statements, immediate and long-
range plans with a priority setting system, will be used as the base 
for formulating a national campaign goal and plan.

object3.OCR:
The Committee is responsible for development of fund raising plans, establishment 
of goals and Heart Fund objectives and establishing standards to guide the conduct 
of campaign activities.

object4.OCR:
Important among these responsibilities is the initiation of a program 
to emphasize the development of "Donor Financial Planning" (DFP) 
programs across the country, to convert into Heart Fund gifts the 
assets of wealthy individuals through either current or deferred giving 
plans.  Since the initiation of the AHA program almost ten Heart 
Associations have established DFP committees for this very purpose.

After more than 15 years of discussion, a fund raising policy that we believe 
to be far more comprehensive, was developed, sent to the Board, thru the regions 
and affiliates and after final revisions by the Fund Raising Advisory and Policy 
Committee, approved by the Board in June 1974.

object2.OCR:
Two years ago, the Fund Raising Advisory and Policy Committee became 
acutely aware that an average 7.7% income growth rate over the past 
five years (exclusive of 1975) is in fact a marginal real growth rate. 
In the absence of any realistic data on which to base national campaign 
goals and objectives, the Fund Raising Advisory and Policy Committee, 
along with the AHA President, asked for and received Board action on 
goals.  Specifically this action calls for all major components 
(National Office, Affiliates, Chapters, Scientific Councils, etc.) 
to set forth a statement of funds needed to support their objectives 
for 1976-'77 and '78.  Based on these statements, immediate and long-
range plans with a priority setting system, will be used as the base 
for formulating a national campaign goal and plan.

object3.OCR:
The Committee is responsible for development of fund raising plans, establishment 
of goals and Heart Fund objectives and establishing standards to guide the conduct 
of campaign activities.

object4.OCR:

to emphasize the development of "Donor Financial Planning" (DFP) 
programs across the country, to convert into Heart Fund gifts the 
assets of wealthy individuals through either current or deferred giving 
plans.  Since the initiation of the AHA program almost ten Heart 
Associations have established DFP committees for this very purpose.

emergency response systems within their companies, including the development 
of response capabilities, education programs alerting employees to symptoms 
of heart attack, delay and denial factors, key employee training, and

object1.OCR:
As reported by Dr. Lawrence M. Herman in the July 20, 1972, issue of the 
Bulletin of the Los Angeles County Medical Association, "About 20% die before 
treatment can be instituted except by the patient or someone present at the 
onset."  Dr. Herman further states, "The greatest delay segment represents 
the patient decision time---the time lost before the patient decides to seek 
help."

object2.OCR:
According  to  currently  accepted  statistics,  approximately  50%  of  the  total 
deaths  from  an  acute  coronary  attack  occur  in  the  first  hour.  Pre-hospital 
mortality  from  coronary  disease  accounts  for  over  300,000  deaths  in  the  United 
States  annually,  with  some  125,000  of  those  deaths  occurring  in  the  under  65 
age  group.

object3.OCR:
Since  the  chances  of  a  coronary  accident  are  statistically  greater  in  areas 
of  high  people  concentration,  such  as  large  employee  groups,  appropriate 
responses  and  procedures  for  meeting  the  emergency  of  a  coronary  accident 
should  become  a  part  of  a  total  emergency  procedures  package,  High  rise 
buildings  offer  even  greater  challenges  to  people  charged  with  developing 
procedures  to  meet  medical  emergencies.

We must communicate the importance of pre- natal medical care to all women, especially those with heart disease who wish to become pregnant.

object1.OCR:
After more than 15 years of discussion, a fund raising policy that we believe 
to be far more comprehensive, was developed, sent to the Board, thru the regions 
and affiliates and after final revisions by the Fund Raising Advisory and Policy 
Committee, approved by the Board in June 1974.

object2.OCR:
Two years ago, the Fund Raising Advisory and Policy Committee became 
acutely aware that an average 7.7% income growth rate over the past 
five years (exclusive of 1975) is in fact a marginal real growth rate. 
In the absence of any realistic data on which to base national campaign 
goals and objectives, the Fund Raising Advisory and Policy Committee, 
along with the AHA President, asked for and received Board action on 
goals.  Specifically this action calls for all major components 
(National Office, Affiliates, Chapters, Scientific Councils, etc.) 
to set forth a statement of funds needed to support their objectives 
for 1976-'77 and '78.  Based on these statements, immediate and long-
range plans with a priority setting system, will be used as the base 
for formulating a national campaign goal and plan.

object3.OCR:
The Committee is responsible for development of fund raising plans, establishment 
of goals and Heart Fund objectives and establishing standards to guide the conduct 
of campaign activities.

object4.OCR:
Important among these responsibilities is the initiation of a program 
to emphasize the development of "Donor Financial Planning" (DFP) 
programs across the country, to convert into Heart Fund gifts the 
assets of wealthy individuals through either current or deferred giving 
plans.  Since the initiation of the AHA program almost ten Heart 
Associations have established DFP committees for this very purpose.
